A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpatialVID and are fully readable, including figures, tables, equations and v2's Appendices A–C. Much of v1's main-text documentation can be matched to material relocated into v2's supplement.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset statistics, caption analyses, camera-estimator trajectory comparisons and comparisons with processed Panda70M videos, including Figures 6, 11 and 13.

after.justification: v2 retains original dataset analyses and adds camera-controlled generation, novel-view synthesis and pose-estimation experiments, with quantitative results in Tables 2–4 and supplementary qualitative results.

M1.justification: The core filtering, MegaSaM/depth/SAM2 annotation and Gemini/Qwen captioning procedures are retained. Section 5.1 and Appendix C.1 add a downstream adaptation of ReCamMaster-style camera conditioning to Wan2.2, excluding intrinsics and injecting learned extrinsic embeddings into transformer blocks.

E1.justification: v2 expands from dataset and annotation assessment to three downstream tasks. Actual training/evaluation now includes RealEstate10K and Sekai-Real for generation, DL3DV for novel-view synthesis, and Sintel, TUM-dynamics and Dycheck for pose estimation, alongside SpatialVID. Earlier citations or dataset-description rows did not constitute these experiments.

E2.justification: New comparisons evaluate Wan2.2-based generators trained on RealEstate10K, Sekai-Real and SpatialVID-HQ; GS-LRM trained on alternative datasets; and CUT3R/VGGT controls for SpatialVID fine-tuning or data inclusion. The earlier six-method annotation comparison is retained as Figure 10. Cited methods such as Long-LRM are not separately evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 introduces task-specific metrics, training budgets and held-out evaluation protocols, including 100/300/500 generation test sequences and equal-size 60K-clip reconstruction training with two input and four target views. The stated preprocessing resolution changes from 1920×1080 to 1280×720. These are reported settings; the PDFs do not establish that earlier analyses were rerun. GS-LRM initialization remains inconsistent between Section 5.2's fine-tuning description and Appendix C.1's training from scratch.

E4.justification: v2 adds a controlled VGGT comparison with and without SpatialVID-HQ training data, plus qualitative examinations of camera adherence, scene details and reconstruction consistency in Figure 6 and Appendix C.2. These extend the analysis beyond the retained filtering, caption-refinement and estimator-selection examples, without introducing a broad sensitivity or robustness study.

E5.justification: Both versions report aggregate statistics and distribution plots without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2's averages over test sequences do not introduce uncertainty estimation; the new sample counts concern evaluation design.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 introduce downstream results absent from v1. For example, v2 reports DL3DV PSNR of 27.80 for SpatialVID-trained GS-LRM versus 27.01 for RealEstate10K training, and TUM-dynamics CUT3R ATE of 0.040 after fine-tuning versus 0.049. Reported HQ size changes from 371,270 clips/1,146.06 hours to 365,362 clips/1,111.55 hours. The retained rotation and translation distributions also exchange metric labels in Figure 5, changing their reported numerical assignments without establishing recomputation.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds an explicit reconstruction-objective definition combining weighted MSE, LPIPS and depth-smoothness losses, which is absent from v1. This is a limited mathematical addition for the new validation experiment. The existing trajectory-metric definitions are retained, and neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The largest-dataset claim and three principal dataset contributions remain. v2's abstract, introduction and conclusion additionally assert experimentally demonstrated effectiveness across controllable generation, world simulation and geometric reconstruction, strengthening the earlier largely prospective application claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of downstream generalization and attributes VGGT's limited Dycheck response to strong pretraining and near-ceiling performance. It newly acknowledges non-metric pose properties and suboptimal masks in complex scenes. Most other MegaSaM failure conditions already appeared in v1 and are consolidated into Section 6.

D1.justification: v2 supplies full captioning prompts and pose-encoding instructions in Figures 11–12, plus checkpoints, trainable/frozen modules, optimizers, schedules, loss weights and hardware for downstream experiments in Section 5 and Appendix C.1. Some earlier information is omitted, including the four-anchor SAM2 detail and the project URL printed in v1; URL omission does not establish resource unavailability.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion or citations for Context as Memory, GameFactory, Wan, T5, VBench and Long-LRM, while removing references such as MotionSight, LGM and LVSM. The central positioning around bridging semantic video datasets and geometric datasets, including Sekai as concurrent work, remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work and curation descriptions are extensively condensed and rewritten. Detailed filtering and semantic analyses move into Appendices A–B, a validation section is inserted, and the conclusion becomes a discussion-and-limitations section. This substantially reorganizes the narrative beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, relocates and enlarges many retained figures, and adds three result tables, prompt panels and downstream qualitative comparisons. The dataset-quality panels are rearranged, with rotation/translation distributions reassigned to different labels. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Tables 2–4 address v1's central evidential gap: downstream usefulness was asserted largely from dataset statistics rather than demonstrated through model training. The new evaluations, including equal-size reconstruction comparisons, and detailed prompts/training documentation substantially strengthen validation and reproducibility. Claims of improvement across all VBench metrics exceed Table 2, and GS-LRM initialization and motion-plot labeling remain ambiguous, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial addition of direct evidence.
